stem.en: The government sets a highest price for wheat of ₹20 per kg, while the market price is ₹30 per kg. What is likely to happen over the next few seasons?

text.en: Farmers grow less wheat, and there may be a shortage.
Farmers grow more wheat, because more buyers now want it.
Nothing changes, because the market price is still ₹30.
Buyers want less wheat, so a surplus of wheat is left unsold.

explanation.en: At ₹20 farmers earn less than at the market price of ₹30, so they may grow less. Buyers want more at the lower price. Less is offered and more is wanted, so there may be a shortage. Farmers may also stop spending on better seeds or irrigation.

hints.en: At a lower price, does a seller offer more or less?
